articles.title: The webhook testing trap I kept falling into (and the 24h fix)
articles.excerpt: I kept burning hours debugging webhook integrations. The pattern: wire up a GitHub push event handler, deploy, push a test commit, and... nothing. Was my signature check wrong? Was the payload malform…
articles.body: I kept burning hours debugging webhook integrations. The pattern: wire up a GitHub push event handler, deploy, push a test commit, and... nothing. Was my signature check wrong? Was the payload malformed? Turns out GitHub was delivering fine and my parser was choking on a field I didn't expect. The usual workaround is a public webhook inspector, but pasting real payloads into a third-party page felt wrong for anything with tokens in headers. So I built an ephemeral receiver: one POST creates a single-use HTTPS URL, catches anything sent to it for up to 24 hours, stores up to 100 events in memory, and auto-deletes on expiry. No account needed on the sending side, no persistent storage to leak. The gotcha that bit me: in-memory means a process restart wipes pending events.

articles.title: Hetzner Unpaid Invoice: What It Means and How to Handle It
articles.excerpt: This article first appeared on Invoala. A Hetzner unpaid invoice means Hetzner's billing system hasn't recorded a successful payment for a billing period by the date it was due. In practice that's usu…
articles.body: This article first appeared on Invoala . A Hetzner unpaid invoice means Hetzner's billing system hasn't recorded a successful payment for a billing period by the date it was due. In practice that's usually a failed card charge, an expired card on file, an expired direct-debit mandate, a bank transfer that arrived without your customer number in the reference, or a payment method that was removed. It does not automatically mean your account is gone — but it does mean you should act on it within days, not weeks, because Hetzner's next step is typically a payment reminder, then restriction of services. Below is what to check first, what happens if you ignore it, and how to sort out the paperwork so the same thing doesn't bite you again.

articles.title: AI Regression Testing Tools for APIs: What the AI Actually Does
articles.excerpt: Search for the best AI regression testing tools and you’ll notice something odd pretty fast. Almost every list is about screens. Self-healing locators, visual diffs, agents clicking through a browser.…
articles.body: Search for the best AI regression testing tools and you’ll notice something odd pretty fast. Almost every list is about screens. Self-healing locators, visual diffs, agents clicking through a browser. Great stuff if your problem is a flaky checkout page. Not so helpful if your problem is an API that keeps breaking clients in ways nobody notices until production. And “AI-powered” has become one of those labels that means a dozen different things. One tool uses AI to write tests. Another uses it to fix them. Another just explains why a test failed. So rather than ranking tools by how loudly they say “AI,” it’s way more useful to ask a plainer question. When you point an automated regression testing tool at an API, what is the AI actually doing for you?

articles.body: CVE-2026-108452: turning SharePoint exposure data into a patch decision Security teams often have two incompatible numbers for the same vulnerability: a large external Exposure count and a much smaller internal list of confirmed affected hosts. CVE-2026-108452 exposes that gap. The Microsoft SharePoint product fingerprint is common, while the specific fixed build and deployment edition are not visible from a general internet scan. Confirmed facts Microsoft lists CVE-2026-108452 as a CWE-22 path traversal issue in Microsoft Office SharePoint. articles.body: A new approach known as “reverse game theory” aims to create incentives for powerful AI models that make following the rules the most rational choice. As AI models become more capable, safety researchers are scrambling to ensure they are “aligned” with human desires—to make sure, in other words, that rogue agents don’t break the law, hack into unauthorized servers, or release poison gas into major cities and kill us all. Until now, this work has mostly focused on trying to peer into an AI’s “brain” to understand what it is “thinking,” or training models to hew to values that we hold dear. Claude, for instance, has its constitution —a sort of moral code.

articles.body: Created by LeSean Thomas and Studio Mir, who both worked on The Legend of Korra , Bass X Machina is a reimagining of the story of Bass Reeves (Brian Tyree Henry), an escaped slave who worked in Indian Territory as a deputy U.S. Marshal. Reeves’ real life was extraordinary, and is said to have inspired the character of the Lone Ranger, but Bass X Machina also gives him a cybernetic arm that shoots magic bullets. The criminals he fights get even bigger upgrades, and the stakes can at times escalate to truly ludicrous levels. Henry does an especially great job expressing exasperation as Bass faces plenty of absurd foes, like an outlaw in a rampaging bull mech that requires complex cooperation to take down.

articles.body: 6 Min Read Happy 65 Years: NASA’s Johnson Space Center Then and Now View of the Manned Spacecraft Center during construction in 1963. Sixty-five years ago, a bold vision took root in Houston: a NASA center dedicated to human spaceflight. Since its founding, NASA’s Johnson Space Center has helped lead the nation’s human spaceflight program, supporting missions from Project Mercury through Artemis. Today, Johnson serves as NASA’s Center of Excellence for Human Spaceflight, and its workforce is helping to usher in a Golden Age of innovation and discovery. Johnson is home to America’s astronaut corps, the Mission Control Center, and the teams behind some of humanity’s greatest achievements in space.
